newsitem.title: CANADA: Regulator says Doman appeal right limited.
newsitem.headline: Regulator says Doman appeal right limited.

text.p: The British Columbia securities regulator denied Friday that the chief executive of Doman Industries Ltd will be allowed to appeal his conviction on insider trading charges.
Earlier Marvin Storrow, who represents Doman chief executive Herb Doman, said the British Columbia Court of Appeal had ruled that Doman could challenge that finding.

But British Columbia Securities Commission lawyer Joe Arvay said a court ruling Friday confirmed that "the finding of liability with regard to the sale of shares is not going to be an issue." He said the ruling was final and there was no way for Doman to be cleared on that charge.
Contacted later, Storrow said Arvay's interpretation was "absolute nonsense."
Both sides agreed that the court granted Doman leave to appeal the punishment on the grounds that Doman was not allowed to make submissions before the penalty was handed down.
The British Columbia Securities Commission in August ruled that Doman, former British Columbia premier Bill Bennett and his brother Russell Bennett were found guilty of insider trading.

The three were barred from trading securities and serving as officers or directors of a public company for 10 years. The court previously ruled that Doman could remain in his post while an appeal was pursued.
A date for an appeal has not been set yet.
The insider-trading case revolved around the collapse in 1988 of a takeover bid by Louisiana-Pacific Corp for Doman Industries.

Herb Doman was accused of passing along a tip to Russell Bennett that the takeover had fallen through. The Bennetts sold all their Doman shares minutes before trading was halted for the announcement of the news. Regulators said the Bennetts made a C$2 million profit.

Doman and the Bennetts vehemently denied the allegations. They were acquitted of similar charges in 1989. Regulators pursued the case through an eight-year legal battle that went all the way to the Supreme Court of Canada.
